short: The last Timurid prince of Central Asia, who lost Samarkand three times and took India instead.
full:
Babur was eleven when his father died in 1494 and left him the small principality of Fergana. Timurid on his father's side and Genghisid on his mother's, he spent his twenties trying to make that inheritance into Timur's: he held Samarkand briefly in 1497, again in 1500, and a third time in 1511 with Safavid help, and lost it each time, finally to Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks, who took Fergana as well. In 1504 he seized Kabul with a few hundred followers and held it for twenty years.

From there he raided into Hindustan, and in 1526 defeated the Delhi Sultan at Panipat with field artillery and encircling horse archers, then the Rajput confederacy under Rana Sanga at Khanwa the following year. He found India hot, flat and short of good fruit, and said so at length in the Baburnama, the memoir in Chagatai Turkish that is among the first genuine autobiographies written in the Islamic world. He died at Agra on 26 December 1530 and was later reburied, as he wished, in a garden at Kabul.
